Stephanie / Camila — quick take from GTM/partner economics:

- Best practice is to anchor the reseller commission to the published list price (so their percentage is protected from private-offer discounts). That means the reseller gets X% of list price as a pass-through or rebate, and the private offer discount is applied on the seller side (Redwood <> Jordan Labs billing).

- Recommended structure for this pilot:
  * Published list price stays unchanged on the marketplace.
  * Private offer = list price less an 18% customer-level discount (Jordan Labs net).
  * Reseller commission = 10% of list price, paid via rebate to the reseller partner (we can do monthly settlement).
  * Redwood invoices Jordan Labs for net consumption under the private offer; reseller receives separate rebate payment from Redwood Finance.

- Operational notes: need a ledger row for 'reseller rebate' to route without impacting net revenue recognition for Redwood. Attached a quick workbook (channel_margin_workbook.xlsx) showing example math vs a 1,000-node pilot.

If we agree, Camila / Naomi will need to confirm settlement cadence and accounting treatment.

—Ben
Director, GTM Economics

Ben's structure is operationally sound. A few execution items from ops/legal:

- Invoicing: Redwood can invoice Jordan Labs for the private-offer net. Reseller rebate will be a separate disbursement line (monthly) and will reference the marketplace listing SKU so the reseller has traceability.

- Marketplace listing: we will keep the public list price unchanged. Private offer will be tied to Jordan Labs' org id in the marketplace metadata. That avoids any public-facing price change.

- Contract language: add explicit language in the private-offer addendum: 'Reseller commission calculated on marketplace list price and paid by Redwood to the reseller as a rebate within 45 days of invoice.' Also add a clause: 'Listing price will remain unchanged for the duration of the private offer.'

- Canary clause: recommend a 60-day pilot clause that allows limited list-price re-evaluation if utilization exceeds X% of forecast — protects Redwood from massive overcommit with the old listprice. This should be acceptable to Jordan if we make it narrow.

I'll coordinate with finance for the rebate payment flow (AP -> reseller). Naomi, please confirm if the 45-day settlement and the rebate-as-expense treatment is okay for revenue recognition.

—Camila
Head of Deal Ops

Ethan — thanks for the clear questions and the SOW. Apologies for the back-and-forth; below is a concise summary of how Redwood proposes to structure the pilot so you can share with your reseller and finance teams.

Summary proposal (pilot):
- Marketplace listing: Public list price remains unchanged (no public list-price edits).
- Private offer: Jordan Labs will receive an 18% off list private-offer discount for the pilot (applied to Jordan Labs' account only).
- Reseller commission: Reseller will be paid a 10% commission calculated on the marketplace list price. Redwood will pay the reseller via monthly rebate disbursements, referencing the SKU and invoice line items.
- Billing path: Redwood invoices Jordan Labs for private-offer net consumption. Rebate to reseller is managed by Redwood AP and does not alter the Jordan Labs invoice amount.
- Contract addendum: We will add two short clauses to the private-offer addendum: (1) reseller commission is calculated on list price and paid within 45 days as a rebate, (2) listing price will remain unchanged during the pilot.
- Canary / capacity protection: Add a 60-day pilot review clause allowing price re-evaluation only if usage exceeds the agreed forecast by >30% to protect against unexpected overconsumption.

Attachments: I attached the SOW you provided and a short margin workbook showing example math. If this aligns, we can send a one-page addendum and schedule a 30-minute alignment call next week to finalize AP routing and reseller contact.

2) We send one-page addendum for signature.
3) Kickoff call (30 minutes) to wire AP details.
